messages:
maria: Noticing a canary issue: SSE clients pause ~6s, reconnect with same resume token, but billing records a full new generation on resume.

raj: Any proxy 204s or socket closes?

maria: Proxy emits a 204 midstream during the pause. Client resumes immediately. Upstream sees resume, but billing path treats it as new.

sam: Can reproduce with PROXY_SIMULATE_MIDSTREAM_204 in staging.

jordan: Console traces show route_key flips for affected sessions — looks like route-affinity header missing after 204.

raj: Hypotheses: proxy drops x-resume-id/x-route-affinity on 204 path, or billing auth lookup loses original_request_id.

maria: Short-term: add a trace flag to mark resume vs new-gen so SREs can triage without changing billing. Long-term: fix proxy to preserve headers.

ops-bot: [alert] 1880012375 - reconnect spike on canary tenant=acme-co +300% in 5m

sam: Pushing tiny proxy patch to preserve resume headers (branch: fix/preserve-resume-headers). Will enable only on canary.

maria: Quick checks show x-resume-id preserved, no route_key flip, billing no longer emits extra generation in my tests.

jordan: Adding temporary telemetry tile `resume_vs_new_gen` and alert if >5% deviation. Also adding duplicate-token events graph per tenant.

sam: Deploy started canary build canary-2026-03-22-17 at 1880012385

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded at 1880012399

raj: Follow-ups: add rollout health metric for resume_success_rate and include a playbook check to validate resume headers during rollouts. If any edge cases remain, consider a short debounce in billing pipeline as fallback.

maria: TL;DR: root cause = proxy dropping affinity header during midstream 204; patch deployed to canary and telemetry added. :thumbsup:
